## Definitions

- [statement] OSHA says engineering and work-practice controls should be the primary feasible means of reducing toxic chemical exposure; NIOSH describes source-capture ventilation for volatile printing-press emissions. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.osha.gov/chemical-hazards/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/engcontrols/ecd/detail37.html

## Structure and components

- [statement] CPSC’s small-parts ban covers products intended for children under three, but exempts books and other articles made of paper; entirely paper pieces detached during use-and-abuse testing are also excluded from the small-part test. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Small-Parts-and-Choking-Hazard-Labeling-FAQs · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://www.cpsc.gov/Business--Manufacturing/Business-Education/Business-Guidance/Small-Parts-for-Toys-and-Childrens-Products
- [statement] CPSC permits reliance on component-supplier lead-test evidence only with due care and access to underlying test documentation, including valid testing by a CPSC-accepted laboratory. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Total-Lead-Content
- [statement] Reliance on a component supplier’s lead test or certificate requires due care and access to underlying test documentation; a bare supplier assurance is insufficient under CPSC’s explanation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Total-Lead-Content
- [statement] PrintNinja describes initial custom board-game prices as budgetary and withholds a final quotation until artwork review. Treat an early estimate as provisional and ask for a written quote against the final artwork and component specification. This is its board-game quotation policy, not a universal rule for all card printers. (low confidence) — https://printninja.com/custom-board-game-pricing/
- [statement] Loffler describes paper and staples as excluded from its explanation of click charges. Ask what consumables, parts and maintenance a proposed service rate actually covers, and price the substrate separately unless the written agreement includes it. Do not transfer this supplier description into an assumption about every contract. (low confidence) — https://www.loffler.com/blog/true-cost-of-owning-a-commercial-printer
- [statement] A physical sample must identify its printing process and included finishing. PrintNinja says its assembled game proof can contain digitally printed components that are not color accurate; Kuo Kau says its uncut digital sample uses actual material but excludes coating, varnish and special finishing. (high confidence) — https://printninja.com/proofing-options/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://www.kkplayingcard.com/en/page-5998/Sample-Proof-Guide.html
- [statement] Publisher Frank West reports checking imposed PDF samples for alignment and cut lines, then counting cards and checking order, duplicates and the rulebook component list. This is a documented operator checklist, not evidence that a supplier performs these checks for the customer. (low confidence) — https://thecityofkings.com/news/requesting-samples-from-your-manufacturer/
- [statement] PrintNinja warns that digitally printed components within a physical game proof are not color accurate. Physical delivery alone therefore does not establish an offset-color reference for every component. (low confidence) — https://printninja.com/proofing-options/
- [statement] Publisher Frank West describes checking card counts, ordering and duplicates against the rulebook’s component list. This is a concrete completeness-and-collation check, separate from judging print appearance. (low confidence) — https://thecityofkings.com/news/requesting-samples-from-your-manufacturer/
- [statement] Kylin recommends naming and counting card faces and shared backs in a manifest; publisher Frank West independently describes counting cards and checking order, duplicates and the rulebook component list. (medium confidence) — https://m.kylinmanufactory.com/news/Board_Game_Pieces/Board_Game_Card_Stock_Guide_GSM_Core_Finish_and_Durability.html · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://thecityofkings.com/news/requesting-samples-from-your-manufacturer/
- [statement] Kylin requires a reference and viewing condition for colour tolerances; Tianyi Shengtang says its achievable numeric colour tolerance depends on the specific colour, substrate and structure. Neither passage supplies a universal tolerance for this game. (medium confidence) — https://m.kylinmanufactory.com/news/Board_Game_Pieces/Board_Game_Card_Stock_Guide_GSM_Core_Finish_and_Durability.html · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://tystprinting.com/quality/

## How it works

- [statement] OSHA’s printing-press roll-cleaning case rejects the minor-servicing exception when workers bypass guards and lack effective alternative protection, even when cleaning is routine, repetitive and integral to production. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.osha.gov/etools/lockout-tagout/case-studies/printing-press-roll-cleaning
- [statement] MakePlayingCards’ returns page requests quality-issue contact within 3 days of arrival; its terms describe a 10-day material-and-workmanship warranty. These statements specify different windows and should be quoted separately when agreeing receipt inspection and remedies. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.makeplayingcards.com/guarantee.aspx · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://www.makeplayingcards.com/pay_terms.aspx
- [statement] Tianyi Shengtang describes taking colour readings during production and stopping the press when readings exceed tolerance; it says batch records link finished goods to material, ink, press-run and inspection records. These are supplier-described controls. (low confidence) — https://tystprinting.com/quality/

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Use the same buyer-supplied artwork for demonstrations and request the workflow through finishing. Ricoh describes start-to-finishing demonstrations, while Konica Minolta invites advance submission of the buyer’s files for printed samples. These are manufacturer offers, not independently measured results. (medium confidence) — https://www.ricoh-usa.com/en/production-printing/about/customer-experience-center · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://kmbs.konicaminolta.us/client-engagement-center/
- [statement] Use representative random samples for lot decisions. NIST describes random lot selection; Minitab also recommends random selection representative of the whole lot, including stratification where needed. (high confidence) — https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/pmc/section2/pmc21.htm · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://support.minitab.com/en-us/minitab/help-and-how-to/quality-and-process-improvement/acceptance-sampling/how-to/attributes-acceptance-sampling/before-you-start/data-considerations/

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] PrintNinja’s published defect clause treats a defect rate under 2% as a completed order. Above 2%, it may provide a proportional refund or reprint and ship replacements at its cost, with the refund/reprint choice reserved to PrintNinja. It may require defect documentation and requires reporting within 90 days of delivery. The clause does not explicitly resolve the exact 2% boundary. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://printninja.com/about/terms/
- [statement] PrintNinja’s terms updated July 14, 2022 treat an order with under 2% defective copies as complete; above 2% the stated remedy may be a prorated refund or replacement printing, at its discretion, with defect reports due within 90 days. The passage does not resolve the exactly-2% boundary. (low confidence) (verified as of 2022-07-14) — https://printninja.com/about/terms/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Small-parts warning requirements depend on the product and intended age, including applicable products for ages 3–6; advertising for toys subject to the warning must carry it too. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/Business--Manufacturing/Business-Education/Business-Guidance/CPSC-Labeling-Requirements-Overview · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://www.cpsc.gov/Business--Manufacturing/Business-Education/Business-Guidance/Small-Parts-for-Toys-and-Childrens-Products
- [statement] CPSC says paper and ordinary CMYK process printing inks can avoid third-party lead testing under material determinations; this does not remove the lead-content limit or the obligation to certify compliance. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Total-Lead-Content · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-16/chapter-II/subchapter-C/part-1500/section-1500.91
- [statement] The CMYK lead determination excludes spot colors, non-CMYK inks, inks outside the substrate and specified after-treatment printing; it cannot be extended automatically to every printed finish. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-04) — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-16/chapter-II/subchapter-C/part-1500/section-1500.91
- [statement] CPSC identifies specific choking-warning labeling rules for products containing small parts and intended for children between three and six; that scope should be checked separately from paper exemptions to the under-three small-parts ban. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/Business--Manufacturing/Business-Education/Business-Guidance/CPSC-Labeling-Requirements-Overview · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Small-Parts-and-Choking-Hazard-Labeling-FAQs
- [statement] CPSC says accessible children’s-product components must meet a total lead limit of 100 ppm and paint or similar surface coatings a separate 90 ppm limit. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Total-Lead-Content
- [statement] In a DC-618 operator discussion, Andres reports that later-cut cards have more skew, while tngcas reports replacing rollers to resolve a similar problem. Use these attributed anecdotes to challenge a demo with checks across the whole sheet and run, and to ask about roller maintenance. They do not establish defects, lifetime or failure rates for other machine models. (low confidence) — https://printplanet.com/threads/duplo-dc-618-skewing-in-machine.295010/
- [statement] In an April 2024 PrintPlanet thread, operator COGordon reports double feeding on a Duplo 646 with lighter stock despite service-setting changes. This is a self-reported case on that model and stock class, not a measured failure rate or proof of a defect in another machine model. Use it to justify observing real-stock feeding during the demo. (low confidence) — https://printplanet.com/threads/methods-for-reducing-static-on-duplo-646.294079/
- [statement] PrintNinja cautions that a single domestic digital-offset unit cannot be treated as a one-to-one comparison with its offset product because materials, finishes and binding techniques differ. (low confidence) — https://printninja.com/electronic-proofing-steps/
- [statement] MakePlayingCards tells customers to verify design and order details before submitting: its automated production policy says cancellations and changes cannot be made after submission. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.makeplayingcards.com/guarantee.aspx
- [statement] MakePlayingCards asks customers to report quality issues within 3 days of arrival. Personalized products qualify for return only for a manufacturing error or product defect. A granted remedy can be replacement, refund or account credit after returned items are inspected; the customer is responsible for returning products unused and undamaged. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.makeplayingcards.com/guarantee.aspx
- [statement] MakePlayingCards says cancellations and changes cannot be made after order submission. Its separate terms require written supplier agreement to modified terms, so a buyer should obtain agreement to project-specific acceptance changes before submitting the order. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.makeplayingcards.com/guarantee.aspx · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://www.makeplayingcards.com/pay_terms.aspx
- [statement] Level 99 Games’ support article, modified on 21 Aug, 2023, excludes slight miscuts under 2 mm from replacements for normal minor printing damage. That publisher’s service threshold is not evidence that every game should accept the same dimensional error. (low confidence) (verified as of 2023-08-21) — https://support.level99games.com/support/solutions/articles/65000067116-help-my-game-is-missing-parts-or-was-shipped-with-damage-

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] OSHA requires guarding where operation exposes employees to injury and lists guillotine cutters; the guard must prevent access to the danger zone during the operating cycle, rather than merely warn. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.212 · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/standardinterpretations/2004-04-07
- [statement] UK HSE identifies failure to refit guards as a major cause of printing-industry accidents. This supports guard-restoration checks as an operational concern, rather than establishing a US legal requirement. (low confidence) — https://www.hse.gov.uk/printing/faqs.htm
- [statement] OSHA lists guillotine cutters among machines usually requiring point-of-operation guarding; hand tools for placing or removing material supplement rather than replace required guards. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.osha.gov/etools/machine-guarding/introduction/general-requirements
- [statement] Duplo says application testing produces an emailed report. Request that report and returned sample output as documentary evidence rather than accepting a verbal compatibility assurance. (low confidence) — https://app.duplousa.com/contact/atr.aspx
- [statement] PrintNinja labels one published price configuration as a 54-card poker deck with a printed tuck box. Use that example only for that configuration; obtain a separate quote for the commissioned game instead of scaling an unrelated deck price. (low confidence) — https://printninja.com/printing-prices/card-game-printing/
- [statement] Duplo’s application-testing form says laminated substrates require compatibility testing and promises an emailed results report. Request qualification of the intended finished stock rather than assuming that an accepted paper weight establishes compatibility. (low confidence) — https://app.duplousa.com/contact/atr.aspx
- [statement] For an equipment quote, request a full-system cost schedule rather than relying on the press price or a demonstration calculator alone. Printing Impressions reports that finishing and landed delivery belong in ownership analysis; Konica Minolta describes its demonstration cost review as raw-cost calculators. This is a procurement recommendation, not a measured cost or break-even estimate. (medium confidence) — https://www.piworld.com/article/anatomy-determining-total-cost-ownership-production-inkjet-presses/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://kmbs.konicaminolta.us/client-engagement-center/
- [statement] Panda describes separate approval gates: approved digital proofs precede sampling; approval of the pre-production copy and component samples starts mass production; review and approval of the mass-production copy precedes assembly of the remaining games. Its mass-production copy arrives when production is nearly complete, so this is an assembly checkpoint rather than a promise that printing has not begun. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://pandagm.com/our-process/
- [statement] PrintNinja publishes differently scoped color statements: its general board-game explainer calls CMYK hard proofs accurate, but its component-specific proof specification excludes digital components from color accuracy and its terms disclaim guaranteed matching without ordered spot/Pantone color. Attribute these positions and obtain component-specific acceptance terms rather than treating the general statement as a universal guarantee. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://printninja.com/custom-board-games/board-game-prototyping-and-proofing/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://printninja.com/proofing-options/, https://printninja.com/about/terms/
- [statement] PrintNinja describes soft proofs as layout references rather than reliable previews of printed color. Its electronic-proofing guide explicitly says the screen proof does not establish final colors. (high confidence) — https://printninja.com/about/terms/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://printninja.com/electronic-proofing-steps/
- [statement] Kylin recommends recording conditional approval in a numbered, revision-controlled report, with both parties retaining its signed or acknowledged final version. This supplies a concrete written revision record rather than an ambiguous approval email. (low confidence) — https://www.kylinmanufactory.com/news/Designing_A_Board_Game/Board_Game_Preproduction_Sample_Approval_Guide.html
- [statement] Kylin describes a golden sample as an approved, controlled physical reference retained for production, used alongside written tolerances rather than replacing them. This is manufacturer guidance, not an independently measured quality result. (low confidence) — https://www.kylinmanufactory.com/news/Designing_A_Board_Game/Board_Game_Preproduction_Sample_Approval_Guide.html
- [statement] Acceptance sampling is primarily for deciding whether a lot is likely acceptable, rather than estimating its quality. NIST distinguishes this immediate lot decision from long-run quality control, while QIMA describes AQL as risk management. A passed sample therefore must not be presented as a measured defect rate for the entire shipment. (medium confidence) — https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/pmc/section2/pmc21.htm · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://www.qima.com/aql-acceptable-quality-limit
- [statement] QIMA describes reinspection after corrections are completed to check the batch against the agreed AQL before shipment. This supports a correction-and-verification step rather than treating the first inspection report as final closure. (low confidence) — https://www.qima.com/aql-acceptable-quality-limit
- [statement] Minitab recommends agreeing both AQL and RQL with the supplier; its guidance describes acceptance and rejection probabilistically rather than as certainty. (low confidence) — https://support.minitab.com/en-us/minitab/help-and-how-to/quality-and-process-improvement/acceptance-sampling/how-to/attributes-acceptance-sampling/before-you-start/data-considerations/
- [statement] Kylin recommends new approval after a mill or stock change, rather than accepting a similar marketing name. (low confidence) — https://m.kylinmanufactory.com/news/Board_Game_Pieces/Board_Game_Card_Stock_Guide_GSM_Core_Finish_and_Durability.html

## Facts and statements

- [statement] CPSC classifies a children’s product by primary intended use for children aged 12 or younger, considering reasonable manufacturer statements, marketing, consumer recognition and age-determination guidance; an age label alone does not control classification. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Childrens-Products
- [statement] CPSC treats traditional playing cards and similar games appealing to a general audience as general-use products; child-oriented features or junior packaging can change that classification. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Childrens-Products
- [statement] For toys primarily intended for children aged 12 or younger, CPSC requires applicable third-party testing by an accepted laboratory and a Children’s Product Certificate; the manufacturer or importer must identify applicable toy-standard sections. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Toy-Safety · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Childrens-Products
- [statement] CPSC distinguishes ASTM F963’s under-14 toy scope from the federal third-party-testing threshold for products intended primarily for children 12 or younger. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Toy-Safety
- [statement] CPSC exempts labeling, instructions and producer markings from third-party laboratory testing, while requiring CPC certification of all applicable toy-standard sections. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Toy-Safety
- [statement] Children’s products need permanent tracking information on product and packaging to the extent practicable, including the responsible firm, production date and location, and identifying production information such as a batch or run number. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Tracking-Label · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://www.cpsc.gov/Business--Manufacturing/Business-Education/Business-Guidance/CPSC-Labeling-Requirements-Overview, https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Toy-Safety
- [statement] CPSC distinguishes a toy’s substantive flammability obligations from premarket testing: the FHSA prohibits hazardous flammable children’s toys even though this requirement does not mandate premarket or third-party testing. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Toy-Safety
- [statement] OSHA’s printing interpretation limits the minor-servicing exception to routine, repetitive, integral production work with effective alternative protection. Normal guillotine blade changing requires an energy-control procedure with lockout/tagout and any necessary guarding. (low confidence) (verified as of 2004-04-07) — https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/standardinterpretations/2004-04-07
- [statement] The MBM-hosted manual describes a movable guard and two-hand control as cutting safeguards for IDEAL 6655. (low confidence) — https://mbmcorp.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/TRIUMPH-6655-op-manual-1399.pdf
- [statement] Where OSHA’s Hazard Communication standard applies, employers need a written program for chemical labels, SDSs and training; SDSs must be immediately accessible, and training covers initial assignment and new chemical hazards. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.1200
- [statement] NIOSH identifies inhalation and skin-contact hazards during press cleaning. Its printing LEV example reports vapor and dust measurement reductions of 83 percent and 67 percent; these are case results, not workshop performance predictions. (low confidence) — https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/engcontrols/ecd/detail37.html
- [statement] A NIOSH educational vignette links visual symptoms to an amine-containing additive used with water-based ink. NIOSH calls the story loosely based on evaluations and cautions that its facility-specific recommendations may not generalize. (low confidence) — https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/bulletin/2015/medical-mystery1b.html
- [statement] OSHA’s lithography guidance identifies repeated reaching, pinching, prolonged standing and low-table bending in hand collation; it recommends reachable stacks, adjusted work height, posture variation and reduced exposure time. (low confidence) — https://www.osha.gov/etools/printing-industry/lithography
- [statement] CPSC’s labeling overview still names ASTM F963-17, whereas its Toy Safety FAQ names ASTM F963-23 with an April 20, 2024 effective date. This is a mismatch between the two cited pages, not evidence that both editions currently govern. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/Business--Manufacturing/Business-Education/Business-Guidance/CPSC-Labeling-Requirements-Overview · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Toy-Safety
- [statement] CPSC allows a reusable storage container to satisfy on-product marking for some multi-piece children’s products; it also says there is no tracking-label exemption based on business size. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Tracking-Label
- [statement] NIOSH identifies press-cleaning solvent vapors and skin absorption as printing hazards; its control guidance describes local exhaust that captures vapor near the press and exhausts it outside with replacement air. (low confidence) — https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/engcontrols/ecd/detail37.html
- [statement] In the printing study summarized by NIOSH, local exhaust reduced measured real-time vapor by 83 percent and dust by 67 percent; these are study results, not a guaranteed reduction for another workshop. (low confidence) — https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/engcontrols/ecd/detail37.html
- [statement] For employers using hazardous workplace chemicals, OSHA requires labels, safety data sheets and worker training about hazards and protective measures. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.osha.gov/chemical-hazards/
- [statement] OSHA’s lithography guidance identifies repetitive forceful paper gripping, awkward wrist postures and bending in finishing work; suggested controls include smaller handled stacks, neutral hand postures and adjustable work surfaces. (low confidence) — https://www.osha.gov/etools/printing-industry/lithography
- [statement] Protocol recommendation: give each candidate the same real game artwork and intended substrate, and request a complete sample run through finishing. Ricoh offers start-to-finishing demonstrations, Duplo requires substrate compatibility tests, and a former equipment seller advises bringing customer files to demos. These sources support the test design; they do not demonstrate this game on any machine. (medium confidence) — https://www.ricoh-usa.com/en/production-printing/about/customer-experience-center · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://app.duplousa.com/contact/atr.aspx, https://printplanet.com/threads/new-owner-new-equipment.292427/
- [statement] PrintNinja distinguishes public example pricing from US-delivery quotes: its price table excludes shipping, sales tax and duties, while its order guide describes US quotes as including taxes and duties. Preserve both attributed statements and obtain an itemized destination-specific quote; neither supports assuming every advertised price is landed. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-02) — https://printninja.com/printing-prices/card-game-printing/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://printninja.com/placing-an-order/
- [statement] Protocol recommendation: request a full-system quote covering the press and required finishing, software and service. Duplo explicitly sells the controller PC separately; Loffler lists cutting, collating, coating and laminating among finishing processes; a print-shop discussion advises confirming service and software rates. The sources provide no complete installed-system price for this game. (medium confidence) — https://www.duplousa.com/product/dc-648-slitter-cutter-creaser/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://www.loffler.com/blog/true-cost-of-owning-a-commercial-printer, https://printplanet.com/threads/new-owner-new-equipment.292427/
- [statement] A production-equipment discussion recommends checking whether click charges vary by sheet size and remain fixed for the lease term; another print-shop operator recommends checking minimum-usage fees. Ask suppliers to write the charging basis and minimums into their quotes. These are historical purchasing cautions, not current market rates. (low confidence) — https://printplanet.com/threads/new-owner-new-equipment.292427/
- [statement] Duplo publishes a maximum DC-648 speed of 40 sheets per minute. This is a manufacturer sheet-processing rating, not demonstrated finished-game output. Protocol recommendation: time the whole sample workflow, including setup and downtime, and count completed decks; Ricoh offers workflow demonstrations and Loffler identifies setup and downtime as costs. (medium confidence) — https://www.duplousa.com/product/dc-648-slitter-cutter-creaser/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://www.ricoh-usa.com/en/production-printing/about/customer-experience-center, https://www.loffler.com/blog/true-cost-of-owning-a-commercial-printer
- [statement] Duplo’s DC-648 page identifies a separately sold PC Controller. Ask the written equipment quote to name the supplied controller configuration and price any required computer explicitly. (low confidence) — https://www.duplousa.com/product/dc-648-slitter-cutter-creaser/
- [statement] Printing Impressions advises checking warranty and service exclusions, separate software/DFE contracts and upgrade costs before closing. Recommended quote protocol: require these coverage boundaries and recurring charges in writing. The article is historical industry reporting, not a current vendor service offer. (low confidence) — https://www.piworld.com/article/anatomy-determining-total-cost-ownership-production-inkjet-presses/
- [statement] Freeze card count, material, finish and packaging in the request for quote. PrintNinja’s guide explicitly asks about those specifications, and its public price examples identify a particular deck and box configuration. Treat the commissioned game configuration as a separate custom request; do not reuse an example-deck price as its quote. (medium confidence) — https://printninja.com/game-quote-guide/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://printninja.com/printing-prices/card-game-printing/
- [statement] Recommended comparison protocol: send one unchanged job specification and identical artwork to each candidate; request returned samples and a written account of the tested stock and workflow. The basis is the vendors’ own-file demonstrations and substrate qualification, not evidence that these suppliers have already produced this game successfully. (medium confidence) — https://kmbs.konicaminolta.us/client-engagement-center/ · keywords: Game print production proofing quality acceptance and safety · also: https://app.duplousa.com/contact/atr.aspx
